items.title: Relative accuracy of AI forecasts with fewer prompt inputs
items.caption: Table 8: Relative accuracy of AI forecasts with fewer prompt inputs
notes: The table shows the accuracy of AI forecasts generated by prompts that provide less information relative to the accuracy of baseline AI forecasts (ratio). Forecast accuracy is computed as mean absolute errors, i.e., the average of absolute differences between realized values and the median human or AI-generated SPF forecasts across survey quarters. The “Generic” forecast uses a prompt that does not provide forecaster characteristics, but does provide real- time data and past median SPF forecasts. The “Generic, w/o real-time data” excludes both forecaster characteristics and real-time data from the prompt. “Generic, w/o real-time data, w/o past SPF data” excludes all data from the prompt including forecaster characteristics, real-time data, and past median SPF forecasts. Finally “Recall” prompts the model to recall values from the training data rather than forecasting values. Values exceeding one (boldfaced) indicate less accuracy compared with the baseline AI forecaster seeded with forecaster characteristics, real-time data, and past median SPF forecasts. Randomized tests evaluate whether values are significantly different from one. The tests are based on 10,000 random draws. Significance levels: ⋆ p-value≤0.10, ⋆⋆ p-value≤0.05, ⋆⋆⋆ p-value≤0.01.

items.title: AI Forecast Performance During Unexpected Events
items.caption: Table 9: AI Forecast Performance During Unexpected Events
notes: The table shows the performance of AI forecasters during seven unexpected events occurring immediately before or after the deadline of the SPF survey (days after survey deadline denoted in parenthesis after the event date). The table reports average Z-scores, measuring the difference between the event-period forecast error and the mean forecast error across the full sample, divided by the standard deviation of the full-sample forecast error. Z-scores near zero indicate typical forecast difficulty, while highly negative values (e.g., <-1) would indicate suspiciously accurate predictions suggesting look-ahead bias. The Z-scores are averaged across the relevant variables for each event and across all variables.

items.title: Reasoning Categories by Economic Period
items.caption: Table 12: Reasoning Categories by Economic Period
notes: Percentage of forecaster responses containing each reasoning type. Categories are non-exclusive. Detailed categories: Mechanical (trends, historical patterns, mean-reversion); Policy (Fed actions, fiscal/monetary policy); Model (eco- nomic theory such as Phillips curve, Okun’s law); Event (specific shocks or crises). ECB aggregation: Following ECB methodology, Model-Based combines Mechanical ∪ Model; Judgment-Based combines Policy ∪ Event. All differences between crisis and normal periods are statistically significant (p < 0.001).
